instruction.text: America consists of two continents. Drag the continent names to label the map.
Complete the statements about the geography of North America.

atoms.b: North America is connected to only one other continent: ((++South_America Antarctica)).
Around North America, you will find the ((++Arctic Atlantic)) Ocean to the north, the Pacific Ocean to the west and the Atlantic Ocean to the ((++east south)).
The cities with the most inhabitants in North America are Mexico City and ((++New_York Alaska)).

instruction.text: Read the text about the climate zones of North America.

text: There are five major climate zones on Earth: tropical, dry, temperate, continental and polar. Each zone makes up an area where temperatures and weather are fairly similar.
hint.label: Climate zones

atoms.text: North America also has very different climate zones. The northern US state of Alaska lies in the icy polar zone.
Much of the USA has a temperate climate with warm summers and cold winters. In southern North America, for example in Mexico, there are both deserts and tropical climates.

instruction.text: Where in North America are these landscapes found? Match them correctly.

hint.text: The blue zones have very cold temperatures. The green area shows a temperate climate. Deserts and tropical rainforests are found in the yellow and orange zones.
hint.sound: The blue zones have very cold temperatures. The green area shows a temperate climate. Deserts and tropical rain-forests are found in the yellow and orange zones.

instruction.text: Drag the marker to the place where North and South America are connected.

feedback.end: Here you can find the country of Panama. It forms the bridge between North and South America.

instruction.text: Complete the statements about the geography of South America.

atoms.b: In the ((++north south)), South America is connected to North America.
The city with the most inhabitants is located in Brazil and is called ((++São_Paulo Amazonas)).
South America is known for the vast Amazon ((++rainforest steppe)) in the north of the continent.
The ((++Amazon Andes)) river flows through the rainforest. Together with the Nile in Africa, it is one of the longest rivers in the world.

instruction.text: Read the text about the Amazon rainforest.

atoms.text: The Amazon rainforest is home to a particularly large number of plant and animal species — many of which have not yet been discovered! Furthermore, the rainforest is very important for the global climate because it absorbs the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

instruction.text: Which three animals live in the Amazon rainforest?

feedback.wrong: Kangaroos do not live on the South American continent, but in Australia in Oceania.
